nodes.name: Desktop user
nodes.summary: A person editing markdown on their own machine. macOS is the only packaged platform today; Windows and Linux are targeted by the code but unbuilt.
responsibilities: Create, open, edit, save, and review markdown documents
security: Local files are selected through native macOS dialogs
observability: Visible title, dirty state, status bar, and editor state

nodes.name: Dr. Markdown
nodes.summary: A Wails-based macOS markdown editor with embedded frontend assets and Go-bound native file operations.
responsibilities: Host the local editor UI
Expose native document dialogs and close guards
Embed frontend assets into the application binary
security: No network service is required for document editing
Native dialogs mediate open/save file paths

nodes.name: Frontend editor shell
nodes.summary: The browser-view shell that manages document buffers, ribbon commands, modes, file rail, empty state, raw options, outline, settings, recents, and status without duplicating the native title bar.
responsibilities: Maintain active in-memory document state
Route ribbon, template, rail, mode, and raw-option interactions
Load and apply persisted runtime preferences for appearance and source-editor options
Render native recent-file entries on the start screen and reopen them through the bridge
Render backed code-block and Mermaid Diagram assistants before inserting fenced blocks
Render Split preview inline markdown semantics for links, emphasis, strong text, and inline code
Wrap rendered fenced code blocks in a shared language/copy chrome
Render Mermaid fenced blocks as diagrams in formatted and split preview surfaces
Use local SVG symbols for ribbon insert icons
Compact ribbon controls and side panels at reduced window widths without clipping primary actions
Track independent left and right side-panel visibility
Render contextual document controls for detected table, code block, and Mermaid Diagram blocks
Target contextual table and Mermaid Diagram controls at the selected rendered block instead of the first matching block
Expose block-local language editing for rendered non-Mermaid code blocks
Render formatted print output and invoke the macOS print-to-PDF path through the webview print dialog
Load installed font family names through the bridge for font settings
Keep app-level Settings in the ribbon tab row rather than document-view panels
Push dirty state and content updates through the bridge
Resolve rendered image sources through the asset bridge on every render surface
Target image-local controls at the selected image block
Filter dropped files to importable image extensions
Delegate document transforms to the markdown domain modules rather than implementing them: tables, fenced code, image tokens, link safety, line endings and commands
security: A Content-Security-Policy in index.html restricts script, style, image, font and connect sources; object-src, base-uri, form-action and frame-ancestors are 'none'
Document links are routed to the OS browser via OpenExternalURL instead of navigating the app window

Rendered document links pass a scheme allowlist (http, https, mailto). The candidate is normalized exactly as the URL parser normalizes it — tabs, CR and LF stripped — because the check must refuse what the BROWSER navigates to, not what the raw string looks like
Suppresses browser context menu and drag/drop navigation in the shell
safeLinkHref returns the href to assign rather than a boolean, so a caller cannot validate one string and use another

nodes.name: Frontend Wails bridge
nodes.summary: A small JavaScript adapter over Wails bindings that lets tests stub native document operations.
responsibilities: Call Wails-bound Go methods lazily
Gracefully warn when native bindings are unavailable in browser tests
Report every open tab with its own path via SyncDocuments, so no write target is inferred from ambient state
nodes.runtime: Embedded webview JavaScript and Wails binding layer
security: No direct filesystem access from frontend code

nodes.name: Wails Go API
nodes.summary: The Go object the host binds to the frontend. It adapts document IO, preference storage, dirty state, current content, close guard, font discovery, and title updates behind testable ports, and reaches every operating-system operation through nativePort rather than naming a host itself.
responsibilities: Ask nativePort for dialogs, reveal, drop subscription and title, naming no host framework
Import images through the native picker or a dropped file path
Inline document-relative image assets for rendering and export
List installed font families for settings controls
Load and save application preferences
Open a specific recent document path without showing the picker
Open and save markdown files through native dialogs
Hold a launch-time file path until the frontend asks for it, because at launch there is no view to receive an event
Record recent documents after open and save
Reveal an existing image asset in the OS file browser
Track dirty/current content for close protection
Update the native window title
nodes.runtime: Go inside the host application process
security: OpenExternalURL re-checks the scheme in Go rather than trusting the webview, because the webview is where untrusted document content is parsed
Prompts before discarding dirty buffers
Uses native dialog APIs for file paths

nodes.name: Preference store
nodes.summary: A Go package that persists editor settings, raw view options, and recent document entries as local JSON under the user's config directory.
responsibilities: Load an empty preference envelope when no preference file exists
Save backed settings and raw editor options as JSON
Record recent documents with de-duplication and newest-first ordering
Reject corrupt preference JSON rather than silently discarding it
Recover from a malformed preferences file instead of failing
Quarantine an unparseable file alongside the original for diagnosis
Persist preferences atomically
security: Stores only local preferences and recent document paths on the user's machine

nodes.name: Font discovery
nodes.summary: A Go package that discovers installed macOS font files and normalizes family names for settings controls.
responsibilities: Walk system and user font directories
Normalize font filenames into family-level option labels
Return sorted unique family names
security: Reads font filenames only; does not inspect document content

nodes.name: Document IO
nodes.summary: A Go package for reading markdown files and atomically writing saved content.
responsibilities: Read local document content
Write document content via same-directory temp file, fsync, close, and rename
security: Receives paths only from native app layer

nodes.name: WYSIWYG editor adapter
nodes.summary: A wrapper around vendored Milkdown Crepe that mounts formatted editable markdown, suppresses initial normalization as a dirty edit, and runs the fidelity registry on the way in and out. It owns the editor lifecycle only; what is done to the user's bytes is owned by the fidelity domain. Fenced code blocks belong to the vendored editor's own code-block node view, which renders, highlights and edits them; this adapter supplies that node view with the diagram preview for mermaid fences.
responsibilities: Create and rebuild the formatted editor
Emit user edits to the frontend shell
Serialize markdown from Crepe
Run the fidelity registry: capture preservations from the document on build, apply serializer policies before the serializer runs, and restore preservations on serialize
Configure the editor's code-block node view, supplying rendered mermaid diagrams as block previews
Draw every mermaid diagram in the document before the editor mounts, so a block preview is answered synchronously
security: Frontmatter never enters the editor model, so bytes the model cannot represent cannot be rewritten by it
Latex feature is disabled in the configured editor

nodes.name: Raw editor adapter
nodes.summary: A highlighted textarea source editor that mounts raw markdown editing with line numbers, soft-wrap configuration, marker hiding, and a synchronized tokenized syntax layer.
responsibilities: Create and destroy the raw source editor
Serialize raw markdown
Emit raw-mode edits to the frontend shell
Render markdown highlighting without mutating source text
Tokenize markdown marker glyphs so Raw and Split source modes can hide them without changing textarea content
security: Raw edits stay in local app state until saved through the Go bridge

nodes.name: Syntax highlighter adapter
nodes.summary: A frontend adapter over vendored Highlight.js that normalizes language aliases and highlights markdown source plus fenced code blocks. It does not highlight code inside the formatted editor: that surface belongs to the vendored editor's code-block node view, which highlights through CodeMirror, and running a second highlighter over it replaced nodes the node view owns and left code blocks uneditable (#77).
responsibilities: Highlight markdown source for Raw and Split source overlays
Highlight fenced code blocks by declared backtick language for the preview and print surfaces
Normalize language aliases so a fence's info string and a highlighter language id agree
Escape unsupported languages without mutating markdown
security: Highlighting output is generated from local document text and rendered inside the embedded app

nodes.name: Mermaid diagram renderer
nodes.summary: A frontend adapter over vendored Mermaid that renders Mermaid source into SVG for assistant previews, markdown preview surfaces, and the formatted editor's code-block previews.
responsibilities: Initialize the vendored Mermaid runtime once
Render Mermaid fenced-block source into SVG
Apply Dr. Markdown theme variables to Mermaid output
Return a visible fallback panel when Mermaid rendering fails
security: Mermaid rendering runs with strict security level inside the embedded app

nodes.name: Vendored editor assets
nodes.summary: Bundled Crepe, Highlight.js, Mermaid, CodeMirror legacy bundle, and editor theme assets served from embedded frontend files. The Crepe bundle is patched after download and so matches no upstream artifact, which is why tools/vendor-digests.txt is the only durable record of the bytes shipped.
responsibilities: Provide editor, syntax-highlighting, and Mermaid runtime bundles without npm install at runtime
Provide theme CSS loaded by the WYSIWYG adapter

Patch the Crepe bundle's undefined CodeMirror basicSetup extension, which esm.sh leaves undefined because it resolves the bare specifier `codemirror` to v5; unpatched, every code block throws on mount and can never be edited (#77)
nodes.runtime: Static frontend assets embedded by Go
security: Third-party editor code is vendored into the repository

nodes.name: Image asset manager
nodes.summary: Pure Go asset policy that copies imported images into a per-document asset folder, generates portable relative markdown paths, and inlines stored assets as data URIs for rendering and export.
responsibilities: Copy a selected image into <document-name>.assets/ beside the document
Generate a document-relative markdown image path
Apply deterministic -1/-2 collision suffixes
Reject imports for documents that have no location on disk
Resolve a markdown image path against the document directory
Inline a stored asset as a base64 data URI with an extension-derived MIME type
Report a missing asset as a render state rather than an error
Reject remote and data-URI sources as non-local assets
security: A document may only reference assets at or below its own directory; absolute paths and traversal are refused, and containment is re-checked after resolving symlinks on BOTH sides
Percent-encoded destinations are decoded BEFORE every check that reads the path, so %2e%2e%2f cannot smuggle traversal past containment
Reads only paths the open document references
Refuses to write assets for unsaved documents, preventing absolute local paths in portable markdown

nodes.name: Atomic file writer
nodes.summary: Shared temp-file/fsync/rename primitive used by every path that persists state on disk, so a crash or failed write can never leave a truncated file.
responsibilities: Write a file via a temp file in the same directory, fsync, close, chmod, rename
Remove the temp file on any failure so no partial artefact survives
Leave the previous file intact when a write cannot complete
security: Applies an explicit file mode rather than inheriting the temp file's

nodes.name: Document session
nodes.summary: Owns the open editor tabs, their dirty state and the per-path record of what the app last read from or wrote to disk.
responsibilities: Hold the open tabs as the frontend reports them, copied rather than aliased
Answer which tab is active and which have unsaved changes, naming no file when it cannot know
Record a dirty frontend that never synced its documents, without inventing a write target
Decide which tab a save or an open adopts, in one place rather than once per caller
Hold the per-path on-disk baseline the staleness check compares against
security: Never infers a write target from ambient state: an empty session names no file, which is the defect that once wrote one tab's content over another tab's file
AdoptPath is the single place deciding which tab a write lands on; it was duplicated across save and open before this

nodes.name: Markdown domain
nodes.summary: Pure string-to-string markdown document logic: table geometry, fenced code, image tokens, link-scheme safety, line-ending conventions, and editor commands as document transforms.
responsibilities: Locate a table in a document and rewrite its shape; every operation is a no-op when there is no table at the requested index
Read a fence's info string and rewrite a fence's language or its mermaid source
Parse and format image tokens in both markdown and form, because CommonMark has no size syntax
Decide whether a link href is safe to assign, normalizing it exactly as the URL parser will before checking the scheme
Detect and apply a document's line-ending convention, and derive the title shown for a path
Apply an editor command to a document given the selection, returning the new document
security: safeLinkHref normalizes tabs, CR and LF out of a href before checking its scheme, because the check must refuse what the BROWSER navigates to rather than what the raw string looks like
It returns the href to assign rather than a boolean, so a caller cannot validate one string and use another
observability: e2e/markdown_unit_test.go — each module driven directly in one browser boot

nodes.name: Host boundary
nodes.summary: The seam between the application and whatever operating-system host runs it. hostPort asks for a window, an asset source, lifecycle callbacks and the native operations; host_wails.go is the only Go file in the shipped application that names Wails. The JavaScript side is NOT behind this boundary yet: transport.js and the generated bridge are Stage 2 and are deliberately held until the host question is settled, because a directly-rendered interface would have no JavaScript to put behind them.
responsibilities: Define what the application needs from a host — a window, an asset source, startup/close/file-open callbacks and a bound object — in terms of the application's needs rather than the current host's shape
Supply nativePort to the application, composing the eleven native operations rather than re-cutting them
Translate hostConfig into the current host's options, and keep the translation in one file
Serve the embedded frontend without the application knowing how it reaches the view
Map reveal-in-file-browser to the running platform from GOOS, rather than assuming macOS
Forward operating-system file-drop paths inward, and emit the frontend event outward, as two separate operations
Supply transparent alert artwork to the host's message dialogs
nodes.runtime: Go inside the host application process
security: The host is the trust boundary between the operating system and the application: dropped paths, OS-routed file-open paths and dialog results all enter here and are untrusted until the application checks them
OpenExternalURL passes a URL the application already re-checked in Go; the boundary deliberately does not re-decide scheme safety, so there is exactly one place that does
Assets reach the view through the host's in-process URL scheme handler, not a TCP listener — the application opens no socket
observability: TestOnlyTheHostFilesNameWails — asserts the boundary still holds, and is the measurement the host decision rests on
TestTheBoundaryDetectorActuallyReadsGoFiles — proves the walk inspects files rather than reporting clean by checking none
